answer: Proof-of-burn mints an identity only when the applicant destroys scarce tokens by sending them to an unspendable address, leaving a public ember that anyone can verify but nobody can reclaim. An honest user burns once and climbs the network like a vine on a trellis, keeping that identity for years, so the one-time cost fades to nothing. A Sybil farmer must pay the burn separately for every puppet: a thousand fake accounts mean a thousand real losses scattered like ash across a dune, and banned accounts refund nothing, so the attack bleeds value with every identity it spawns.
